Hi Sara,

Thanks for the sample — that's perfect. I ran a quick pass with our v1 sizing model and attached the workbook (orca_sizing_model_v1.xlsx). High-level notes below so you have context before we dig in with Marcus:

- Peak observed token rate (60-minute window): ~1.1M tokens/minute inbound + outbound => ~18.3k tokens/sec
- Baseline model variant: gpt-4x-lite (48k context), measured on A100-class dedicated node: ~700–850 tokens/sec per GPU tail-p95 ~240–320ms depending on sequence length mix
- Estimated GPUs for steady peak (keep p95 <= 350ms): 22–26 GPUs (autoscale policy with 10% continuous buffer)
- Marketing surge x3 (10 days): plan for burst pool of +30–40 GPUs (pre-warm to avoid cold-start vectorization penalties). That yields steady-state headroom for short spikes while preserving p95 <= 350ms in our sims.

Caveats and next steps:
- The tokens/sec per GPU above assumes 8-bit quantized variant and sequence-length distribution matching the sample. Long-form prompts raise p95 sharply.
- Marcus will validate the kernel path and recommend specific instance types (we often mix H100 for high throughput and A800 for cost band).

Propose: 30-minute call tomorrow with Marcus + Raj to agree on a commitment band and a canary plan. I added Monica to loop on rollout/ops.

Hannah / Monica / Sara,

I took the sample and ran three scenario sweeps in our sizing model: conservative, recommended, and aggressive. Summary (rounded):

- Conservative (SLO-focused): allocate for steady 1.1M tpm => 28 A100-equivalent GPUs; p95 modeled at ~340ms. Minimal burst capacity; suitable if commit needs to be tight.
- Recommended (cost/latency balance): 24 mixed GPUs (12 H100, 12 A800-equivalent) with autoscale headroom to +30 GPUs for bursts — median p95 ~260ms, burst p95 ~320ms. This yields a 25% cost reduction vs all-H100 while meeting SLOs.
- Aggressive (latency-first): 34 H100-equivalent GPUs pre-warmed => p95 ~200–230ms, headroom for sustained x3 traffic without autoscale. Higher commit cost but simplest operational profile.

Other considerations:
- KV-prefetch and prefix caching could reduce effective tokens/sec by ~8–15% on your chat-heavy endpoints — we can instrument a short pilot to quantify.
- Model quantization and CPU offload settings matter; Monica and I propose a 48-hour canary to measure observed tail before full commit.

I attached the spreadsheet with per-GPU tokens/sec assumptions and cost curves. Will join the call and walk through the numbers.

— Marcus

Raj / Sara — quick answers and next steps (action items below).

- Tokens/sec per GPU (recommended mix): H100-equivalent ~820 tokens/sec; A800-equivalent ~520 tokens/sec. Effective blended average in our model = ~670 tokens/sec once autoscaling and batching are considered. Numbers assume 8-bit quals + KV prefix caching enabled.
- Burst pool behavior: we recommend pre-warming the +30 GPU burst pool for any planned marketing events. Cold-start effects (uncached KV + cold kernels): we simulated a 12–18% p95 degradation in the first 10–15 minutes, then stabilizes as caches fill and kernels JIT. Pre-warming reduces that to ~3–5% degradation.

Proposed commitment band and plan to present to procurement: 
1) Commit band: 20–28 GPUs (mixed H100 + A800) with an on-demand burst pool of +30 GPUs available for up to 14 days per quarter.
2) Canary: 48-hour canary at 50% projected peak to validate p95 and token assumptions (Redwood to share instrumentation hooks).
3) SLA: target p95 <= 350ms for committed baseline; lower latencies guaranteed at higher commit tiers.

Action items:
- Redwood: provide a short doc summarizing tokens/sec per instance and cold vs warm p95 sims (I'll turn Marcus' sheet into a 2-page summary). Attachment: mutual_action_plan_orca.md (I'll drop the doc in the Drive).
- Orca: confirm procurement preference for commit band vs fixed count by EOD Monday; confirm preferred billing cadence.
- Schedule: 30-min sync on Monday 10/18 10:00am PT to finalize the band and canary dates.
